finding: 2026 revenue grew 21.44% but profit grew 16.04%; margin moved -0.6pp to 12.87%.
uncertainty: Bootstrap 95% CI for the margin change is -5.56 to 4.84pp: the overall dip is not distinguishable from normal year-to-year noise.
action: Treat the dip as an early signal and look at where it is concentrated, not as a proven decline.

finding: Margins fell most in Machines (-11.65pp, discount rate +8.16pp), Binders (-9.86pp, discount rate +7.38pp), Tables (-8.42pp, discount rate +5.07pp).
uncertainty: Across all 17 sub-categories, a deeper discount change goes with a larger margin drop (Spearman rho -0.662, p 0.0038). Correlation, not proof of cause.
action: Review the discount policy for these three sub-categories first.

finding: Lines discounted above 20% are 15.7% of revenue but lose $136,009; every discount level from 30% up has a negative margin.
uncertainty: Holding sub-category, region and segment fixed, each extra 10 points of discount goes with -19.89pp of line margin (95% CI -20.3 to -19.47). The dataset is a synthetic Tableau sample, so this describes the sample, not a real retailer.
action: Cap discounts at 20% unless a test shows the extra volume pays for itself.

finding: 304 of 1894 products lose money in total ($77,634, 26.56% of total profit). 12 states/provinces are loss-making overall, led by Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania; Central has the lowest margin (7.9%).
uncertainty: Product-level losses mix discounting, shipping and pricing; the data has no separate cost lines.
action: Start a price/discount review with the top 20 loss-making products and the 3 worst states.

finding: Holt-Winters (best monthly holdout error) projects $735,154 revenue for the next 12 months.
uncertainty: On the 2026 holdout it missed months by 23.25% on average and undershot the year by 20.06%; SARIMA was worse month to month (28.22%) but within 5.91% on the annual total.
action: Use the forecast for seasonal planning (Sep, Nov, Dec run 63-82% above an average month), not for a precise budget.
